title: Stripe reportedly acquires OpenRouter, the AI model router, for over $7bn
excerpt: Stripe has reportedly finalised a deal to buy OpenRouter, the AI gateway that routes traffic to more than 400 models, for over $7bn, a bet that the durable money in AI is in metering and billing.
content_html:
Stripe has, according to Bloomberg, finalised a deal to buy OpenRouter for more than $7bn. The payments giant declined to comment, and the sum is not officially confirmed, but the reported number tells its own story about where the smart money in AI now thinks the durable profit lies.

OpenRouter is what the industry calls an AI gateway, or a model router. In plain terms, it gives developers a single doorway to more than 400 models, and lets them switch between providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google according to price, speed or mood, without rewriting their code or marrying any one lab.

Roughly 8 million users now pass through it, drawn by the promise of never being held hostage by a single vendor’s pricing or downtime. The pitch is neatly captured by chief executive Alex Atallah, who has called OpenRouter “the equivalent of Stripe for AI”, a comparison that reads rather differently now that Stripe has apparently agreed with him.

Which is presumably why Stripe agreed with him and bought it. The logic fits a company that made its fortune not by inventing money but by metering its movement, taking a modest slice every time value changes hands online.

Apply that instinct to a fragmenting model market, where developers juggle a dozen suppliers and hate being locked in, and the appeal of a neutral billing-and-routing layer becomes obvious.

It is the same wager that other infrastructure players are placing on the plumbing rather than the product, as Baseten’s $1.5bn raise on cheap inference made plain earlier this year.

The price is the part that should make you sit up. The Wall Street Journal reported the two sides were in talks back in July; Bloomberg now says the deal is done.

OpenRouter closed a $113m Series B only in May 2026, at a $1.3bn valuation, backed by Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Menlo Ventures and Alphabet’s CapitalG. Three months later, Stripe is reportedly paying more than five times that figure. Markups like that are not paid for revenue. They are paid for position.

And the position here is genuinely strategic. As frontier labs commoditise one another and prices keep sliding, the model itself starts to look like the least defensible link in the chain.

The switching layer, by contrast, gets more valuable the more the market splinters, because someone has to meter, route and bill usage across all of it.

That is the thesis behind bets like IBM’s $240m push into cheap open-source inference, and it is a nervy one for anyone hoping a single model will command lasting rents.

That nervousness is not abstract. The same relentless drive towards the cheapest adequate option, sometimes called thrift-maxxing, is exactly the behaviour OpenRouter industrialises.

Every time a developer swaps a pricey flagship for a cheaper alternative to shave a bill, the router wins and the model loses a little pricing power. Stripe, in other words, is buying the machine that helps customers shop around, which is a rather elegant place to stand.

There are caveats worth keeping, and this being AI, plenty of them. The deal is reported rather than announced, Stripe is saying nothing at all, and regulators on both sides of the Atlantic tend to take a keen interest when a payments behemoth swallows a chokepoint.

Neutrality, too, is a fragile asset; a router owned by one giant may not feel quite as impartial to the labs whose traffic it meters, and some may think twice about routing through a rival’s cash register.

But if the reported figure holds, the message is hard to miss. In the AI gold rush, Stripe has decided the safest bet is not the gold. It is the tolls on the road to the mine.

content_html_zh:
据彭博社报道，Stripe 已敲定以超过 70 亿美元收购 OpenRouter 的交易。 这家支付巨头拒绝置评，这笔金额尚未得到官方确认，但报道的数字讲述了自己的故事，即人工智能领域的聪明资金现在认为持久利润在哪里。

OpenRouter就是业界所说的AI网关，或者模型路由器。 简单来说，它为开发人员提供了访问 400 多个模型的单一途径，并允许他们根据价格、速度或情绪在 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 等提供商之间切换，而无需重写代码或与任何一个实验室联姻。

现在大约有 800 万用户通过它，因为他们承诺永远不会受到单一供应商的定价或停机时间的影响。 首席执行官 Alex Atallah 巧妙地捕捉到了这一点，他将 OpenRouter 称为“相当于 AI 领域的 Stripe”，既然 Stripe 显然同意他的观点，那么这种比较的读法就大不相同了。

这大概就是 Stripe 同意他并购买它的原因。 这种逻辑适合一家公司，该公司不是通过发明货币而是通过衡量其变动来发家致富的，每次价值在网上易手时都会从中获得适度的份额。

将这种本能应用于分散的模型市场，在该市场中，开发人员与十几家供应商周旋，并且讨厌被锁定，中立的计费和路由层的吸引力就变得显而易见。

正如 Baseten 今年早些时候通过廉价推理融资 15 亿美元所表明的那样，其他基础设施参与者也将赌注押在管道而不是产品上。

价格是应该让你坐立不安的部分。 据《华尔街日报》报道，双方早在 7 月份就曾进行过谈判。彭博社现在表示交易已经完成。

OpenRouter 仅在 2026 年 5 月就完成了 1.13 亿美元的 B 轮融资，估值为 13 亿美元，由红杉资本、Andreessen Horowitz、Menlo Ventures 和 Alphabet 旗下 CapitalG 提供支持。 据报道，三个月后，Stripe 支付的费用是这个数字的五倍多。 这样的加价并不是为了收入而支付的。 他们按职位付费。

这里的位置确实具有战略意义。 随着前沿实验室相互商品化以及价格不断下滑，模型本身开始看起来像是链条中最不可靠的一环。

相比之下，市场分裂得越多，交换层的价值就越高，因为必须有人对所有交换层的使用情况进行计量、路由和计费。

这就是 IBM 斥资 2.4 亿美元进军廉价开源推理领域的赌注背后的论点，对于任何希望单一模型能够获得持久租金的人来说，这是一个令人紧张的赌注。

这种紧张感并不抽象。 同样不懈地追求最便宜的适当选择，有时称为节俭最大化，正是 OpenRouter 工业化的行为。

每当开发人员将昂贵的旗舰产品换成更便宜的替代品以节省开支时，路由器就会获胜，而该模型会失去一点定价能力。 换句话说，Stripe 正在购买帮助顾客货比三家的机器，这是一个相当优雅的立场。

有一些警告值得保留，而这就是人工智能，其中有很多警告。 该交易是报道而不是宣布，Stripe什么也没说，当支付巨头吞下一个瓶颈时，大西洋两岸的监管机构往往会表现出浓厚的兴趣。

中立也是一种脆弱的资产。一个巨头拥有的路由器可能对其流量测量的实验室感觉不太公正，有些人可能会在通过竞争对手收银机进行路由时三思而后行。

但如果报道的数字成立，那么这个信息就很难被忽视。 在人工智能淘金热中，Stripe 认为最安全的赌注不是黄金。 这是通往矿井的道路的通行费。
